items.title: The sheafyness condition is equivalent to the right adjoint carrying supported objects to supported objects
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For f : X -> Y a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes with right adjoint a of Rf_*, a quasi-compact open V of Y with inverse image U, the lemma asserts: for every Q in D^+_QCoh(O_Y) supported on Y minus V the image a(Q) is supported on X minus U if and only if equation labelled equation-sheafy is an isomorphism on all K in D^+_QCoh(O_Y); the same statement without the bounded below hypothesis; and that if a commutes with direct sums then the conditions of (1) imply those of (2) (statement lines 1034-1052). For (1) the proof takes K in D^+_QCoh, forms the distinguished triangle K -> Rj_*K|_V -> Q -> K[1] whose third term is quasi-coherent by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-image and is supported on Y minus V, applies a to get a distinguished triangle on X, and observes that if a(Q) is supported on X minus U then restricting to U makes a(K)|_U -> a(Rj_*K|_V)|_U an isomorphism, which is exactly the sheafyness condition; the converse is immediate (proof lines 1054-1074). Assertion (2) is proved in exactly the same way (proof lines 1076-1078). For (3) the proof assumes the conditions of (1), writes T = Y minus V, and notes that the strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory of objects Q in D_{QCoh,T}(O_Y) with a(Q) in D_{QCoh,f^{-1}(T)}(O_X) is preserved by direct sums and hence derived colimits; since D_{QCoh,T}(O_Y) is generated by a perfect object E by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-generator-with-support and E lies in the subcategory by assumption, and since by Derived Categories, Lemma labelled derived-lemma-write-as-colimit every object is a derived colimit of a system whose transition cones are direct sums of shifts of E, induction gives that the subcategory is everything, yielding the conditions of (2) (proof lines 1080-1103). Reducing the unbounded case to a generation statement for complexes supported on a closed subset is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
